disposition_reason: Pak choi, amaranth and caisim leaves from a campus farm in Jengka, Malaysia were analysed for arsenic, cadmium and lead by GFAAS; leaf means are printed in the Results text.

study.design: Farm soil-plant survey with bioconcentration and health risk assessment
study.origin: Farm on a university campus, Jengka, Pahang, Malaysia (03 45 N, 102 56 E); produce sold to local communities
study.market: not purchased; harvested at the farm
study.method: Oven drying at 60 C, mixed-acid digestion, graphite furnace AAS
study.lod_text: Detection limits As 1.00, Cd 0.05, Pb 0.10 mg/kg
study.qa: SRM 1570a spinach leaves and SRM 2711a Montana soil; recoveries 85-110%; triplicate analyses with RSD < 5%

findings.notes: Leaves; mean of the farm samples (30 soil-vegetable sets across three species; per-species n not stated); Figure 1 shows mean ± 5% error

unresolved: Root concentrations (As 0.94-1.67, Cd 0.43-1.52, Pb 0.32-1.81 mg/kg) are for roots not normally eaten and are not recorded as findings; soil values are figure-only.
All leaf arsenic and lead means are below the paper's own stated detection limits (As 1.00, Pb 0.10 mg/kg), so they cannot be reconciled with the method.
Per-species sample numbers are not stated (30 sets in total). Collection dates not reported.
Basis taken as dry because samples were oven dried before digestion; tables do not label it.
